evals.prompt: The header of pure-function nodes in the graph editor (src/NetPrints.Editor/Graph/Nodes/NodeView.axaml) is hard to read in the Light theme. Fix the colors.
evals.expected_output: Light and Dark tokens in ThemeDictionaries in EditorStyles.axaml, referenced with DynamicResource, no color literal in the view (E2, E6, D7).
assertions: Tokens defined per variant in ThemeDictionaries
No hex or named color added to a view

evals.prompt: Add a 'danger' style class for destructive buttons that makes them red in both the light and the dark theme.
evals.expected_output: A Style with Selector Button.danger in EditorStyles.axaml whose setters use per-variant tokens via DynamicResource; lowercase class name (D7, D8).
assertions: No ControlTheme for a color-only change

evals.prompt: Show the compile status (CompileStatus) as a colored dot in the main window toolbar.
evals.expected_output: The dot's color comes from style classes set from the VM state, with each class's style setting a per-variant DynamicResource token; no converter builds a brush. A converter appears only if it maps CompileStatus to an icon kind, and then it is sealed with a static Instance, ConvertBack throws NotSupportedException, unexpected input returns UnsetValue, and a plain xUnit test covers it (D5, D7).
assertions: Color comes from style classes plus per-variant tokens in ThemeDictionaries
No converter returns a brush or color
Any converter maps to an icon kind, is sealed with a static Instance, and ConvertBack throws NotSupportedException
Any converter has a plain xUnit test without an Avalonia app
